name: Caribbean Javanese
sweep_summary: cari1276 Caribbean (Surinamese) Javanese is not in the catalog. The single title-keyword item, Mardiwarsito's 'Prosodi (Cahndah-sastra) bahasa jawa' (Pelangi bahasa, Verhaar festschrift, Jakarta: Bhratara Karya Aksara 1982, pp. 211-266), is not about this language: Glottolog's own record marks the jvn tag as a 'computerized assignment from "jawa"', and chandah-sastra is verse metrics, so it is Javanese verse prosody, not word stress; no open copy exists (print holdings at UGM/Atma Jaya only) and it should not be acquired for stress. Beyond that item I fetched sources and read four open sources on the Suriname variety: Villerius 2018 LOT dissertation (§3.2 Phonology, segmental only, silent on stress), Vruggink 1985a and 1985b in OSO 4(1) via DBNL (state that the sound system does not differ noticeably from Indonesian Javanese per Uhlenbeck 1978; no stress statement), and Rofiq 2025 LITERA (five segmental changes; silent). None gives a word-stress statement, so best_new_statement is found=false. Unread and worth acquiring: Vruggink (& Sarmo) 2001 Surinaams-Javaans-Nederlands woordenboek with its pronunciation sketch (high), Wolfowitz 1983 dissertation / 1991 book (medium), Villerius 2017 De Gruyter chapter and Wolfowitz 2002 Atlas chapter (low).org, Crossref and DBNL.

sources.citation: Rofiq, Zainur. 2025. The phonological changes of Surinamese Javanese: A language contact perspective. LITERA 24(1): 52-60.
sources.quote: The results disclose five phonological alternations: palatal plosive to voiceless and voiced alveolo-palatal affricates, vowel shift from central close-mid to front close, nasal-stop combinations, retroflex to non-retroflex plosive changes, and the change of alveolar nasal to velar nasal in suffixes.
sources.note: Silent on word stress. Reports five segmental alternations (palatal plosive > affricate, vowel shift, nasal-stop combinations, retroflex > non-retroflex, n > ng in suffixes) from 16 Surinamese vs 7 Indonesian Javanese speakers; no mention of stress, accent, or syllable prominence anywhere in the text.

sources.citation: Villerius, Sophie E. 2018. Development of Surinamese Javanese: Language contact and change in a multilingual context. LOT dissertation 528, Radboud University Nijmegen. (Glottolog 578323, dated 2019)
sources.quote: In this respect, the phonology of Surinamese Javanese in my corpus mostly resembles that of Central Javanese: kanca is pronounced [kɔɲcɔ], and kancané is pronounced [kaɲcane].
sources.note: Silent on word stress. Section 3.2 Phonology (pp. 58-60) treats only segments: vowel inventory and the /a/ -> [ɔ] allophony ('In Central Javanese, /a/ becomes [ɔ] in word-final open syllables and penultimate open syllables where a following open syllable has /a/... the phonology of Surinamese Javanese in my corpus mostly resembles that of Central Javanese: kanca is pronounced [kɔɲcɔ]'). Grep of the whole text for stress/accent/penultimate finds no prosodic statement; p. 245 notes phonology is 'not looked at in any case studies in this thesis'.

sources.citation: Vruggink, Hein D. 1985. De spelling van het Surinaams Javaans. OSO: Tijdschrift voor Surinaamse Taalkunde, Letterkunde en Geschiedenis 4(1): 63-72.
sources.quote: Wat het Surinaams Javaans betreft is er nog niet een dergelijke analyse gemaakt. Wel beschikken we over een beschrijving van het klanksysteem van het Javaans in Indonesië (Uhlenbeck, 1978: 23, 24). Aangezien er geen aanwijzingen zijn dat het klanksysteem van het Surinaams Javaans hier wezenlijk van verschilt, kunnen we deze beschrijving veilig als basis nemen.
sources.locator: section 'De fonemen van het Surinaams Javaans', p. 65
sources.note: Silent on word stress. Gives the phoneme inventory (6 vowels, 21 consonants) taken over from Uhlenbeck 1978 for Indonesian Javanese, 'since there are no indications that the sound system of Surinamese Javanese differs essentially from it'; open/closed-syllable vowel allophony only. The only 'accent' hits are orthographic diacritics on e.

sources.citation: Vruggink, Hein D. 1985. Het Surinaams Javaans: een introduktie. OSO: Tijdschrift voor Surinaamse Taalkunde, Letterkunde en Geschiedenis 4(1): 53-62.
sources.quote: Op het gebied van de fonologie zijn, voorzover nu bekend, geen noemenswaardige verschillen aan te wijzen. Wel is er binnen het S.J. enige fonetische variatie, samenhangend met de verschillende dialektachtergrond van de sprekers.
sources.note: Silent on word stress. States that, as far as known, Surinamese Javanese shows no noteworthy phonological differences from Indonesian Javanese, only some phonetic variation by speakers' dialect background. Translation: 'In the field of phonology, as far as is now known, no differences worth mentioning can be pointed out. There is, however, some phonetic variation within Surinamese Javanese, connected with the different dialect backgrounds of the speakers.'
